name: Adam
bio:
Adam is the first human being in the Bible, formed by God's own hands from the dust of the ground; God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and he became a living soul (Genesis 2:7). God placed him in the Garden of Eden to tend it, and brought every living creature to him to be named — showing that God gave humanity the honor and responsibility of ruling over the earth.

## 👤 Identity and Standing: Made in God's Image

Adam was made in the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26-27), the father of the whole human race. Seeing that it was not good for him to be alone, God caused him to fall into a deep sleep and took one of his ribs to form a woman as his companion — establishing the foundation of marriage as "the two shall become one flesh" (Genesis 2:18-24).

## 📖 Core Story: From the Garden to Exile

1. **Obedient Keeper**: God placed Adam in Eden, commanding him to tend and keep it, and gave him a single prohibition — not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for in the day he ate of it he would surely die (Genesis 2:15-17).
2. **The Fall**: The serpent tempted Eve, Eve gave the fruit to Adam, and he ate; the eyes of both were opened, and they knew they were naked (Genesis 3:6-7).
3. **Bearing the Consequences**: When God questioned Adam, he shifted the blame to Eve; God pronounced that the ground would be cursed because of him, that he would toil and sweat for bread all his days, and would return to dust (Genesis 3:17-19).

## ✨ Key Character and Theological Significance

- **Representative of Humanity**: Paul calls Adam "the first man" in the New Testament — his disobedience brought sin and death into the world, standing in contrast to Christ, "the last Adam," who brings life and grace (Romans 5:12-19; 1 Corinthians 15:45).
- **Fall and Hope Together**: Though Adam was driven from Eden, God promised that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15) — the earliest promise in Scripture pointing toward a Redeemer.

Adam's story reminds us that though humanity was made in God's glorious image, disobedience broke the original closeness with God — yet God did not abandon humanity; the promise of redemption was already quietly planted at the very moment paradise was lost.
